sentences.text: For Petitioner : Mr.S.Vinoth Kumar  Government Advocate (Crl  ORDER

This Suo Motu Case is dealt with in an extraordinary manner by the Dedicated Bench, pursuant to Suo Motu.W.P.(Crl.) No.618 of 2025.
2.

This case is registered for alleged offences under Sections 279 and 304(A) of Indian Penal Code,
1860 and Section 181(3) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The incident occurred in the year 2017.
It is reported that the defacto complainant has filed a claim petition and compensation has already been awarded.
Further, it is submitted that the case is presently pending at the stage of summons and there is no previous or subsequent case as against the accused.
The defacto complainant is present before the Court and has stated that he does not want to pursue the case any further.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 24/10/2025 03:35:18 pm ) D.BHARATHA CHAKRAVARTHY, J.
nsl 3.

Considering the factual matrix, context of the case, the antecedents of the accused, the reason for absence from his usual place, and the submission that, despite best efforts, the summons could not be served, it is evident that even if the accused is brought to face trial, it would impinge upon his right to a speedy trial.
Due to the passage of time, a meaningful trial is unlikely, and no useful purpose would be served.
